newsitem.title: USA: Dulles, National Airports generate revenues - paper.
newsitem.headline: Dulles, National Airports generate revenues - paper.

text.p: Washington National and Dulles International airports together generated $5.5 billion worth of business revenue in 1995, substantially more than they did two years before, largely because of growing air service at Dulles and continuing construction at National, the Washington Post reported on Tuesday.
The revenue estimates were part of a report released Monday by the Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority.
The study compares the economic impact of the airports in 1995, the most recent year for which figures are available, and in 1993.

About 12.4 million passengers used Dulles in 1995, up from about 10.8 million in 1993. That increase, combined with the growth in cargo handling, has increased business revenue by 43 percent, to $3 billion, in 1995, the report said.

And 6.3 million of the region's 20 million tourists came via the two airports in 1995, and stayed long enough to spend $4.4 billion on hotels, meals and other things, according to the study, the Post reported.

The $1 billion in long-term reconstruction at National and the equally costly expansion at Dulles have produced most of the job growth at both airports -- nearly 3,000 net additional jobs during the two-year period studied, the Post reported.
That boosted the total number of jobs at the two airports to 25,215 in 1995, up 13.2 percent from 1993.
Dulles Airport is in Fairfax and Loudoun counties and genrated $6.7 million of taxes for Fairfax and $6.4 million for Loudoun in 1995.
And National is in Arlington County and generated $3 million in taxes 1995.
